key_reasoning.reason: Four real components touched across three layers: Application model + CheckConstraint (core/models.py), ApplicationRepository.update_project (repository), ProjectService.update_project plus a new _validate_chargeback_attribution classmethod and VALID_CHARGEBACK_ATTRIBUTIONS allow-list (service, new abstraction), and ProjectVisibilityService list/detail dict-builders (service) feeding the projects.py router's four Pydantic schemas (API).

Initial implementation pass left two gaps that only surfaced in code review and required an actual fix-up round: CR-001 (clearing cost_center_id without resetting chargeback_attribution orphaned a cost_center-attributed project) and CR-002 (chargeback_attribution accepted any unvalidated string, failing only at the DB CHECK constraint as an unhandled 500). This is the rubric's 'rework risk' signature for L, evidenced by a real second commit round (code-review-check.diff) rather than a hypothetical gap.

Closest existing pattern is the prior chargeback_enabled boolean field/update flow (well-established, low risk on its own), but that pattern did not cover the security-sensitive aspect of the new enum-valued field: ProjectUpdateRequest.chargeback_attribution was a bare str with no allow-list, so any value skipped validation and reached the DB constraint as an unhandled exception. Standards review flagged this as a partial security-patterns violation and it was a real blocking finding (CR-002) resolved via a VALID_CHARGEBACK_ATTRIBUTIONS allow-list added in the fix-up commit — the Step 1 divergence-from-precedent auto-bump applies on real evidence, not speculation.

10 unique files touched across the two diffs (9 modified, 1 new): core/models.py, repository/application_repository.py, rest_api/routers/projects.py, service/project/project_service.py, service/project/project_visibility_service.py, one new Alembic migration, and four test files spanning tests/codemie/rest_api/routers and tests/codemie/service/project — 3+ distinct directories, matching the L band (8-10 modified, 3+ directories).

Three distinct layers with a schema change: DB-Persistence (new column + CheckConstraint + Alembic migration with upgrade/downgrade), Service (ProjectService validation/orchestration, ProjectVisibilityService), and API (projects.py request/response schemas and handlers) — the rubric's defining case for L ('3-4 layers including persistence — schema change or migration').

red_flags_applied: Technical Risk: divergence from the closest precedent (chargeback_enabled) on the security-sensitive aspect (input validation) materialized as a real blocking code-review finding (CR-002, standards_review security=partial) requiring a fix-up commit — bumped from the base well-established-pattern score.

Requirements Clarity: two edge cases (orphaned cost_center attribution on clear, unvalidated enum value) were missed in the initial pass and required an actual code-review fix-up round before approval — direct evidence of rework risk.
